html:
Klein-Venedig, Little Venice, was the German name for the province of Venezuela when the Welser banking family of Augsburg governed it, from 1528 to 1546.

The emperor Charles V owed the Welsers huge sums, and gave them the right to conquer and settle the coast in return. Their governors, based at Coro, spent their time on long expeditions into the interior in search of gold and El Dorado. They took Indigenous slaves and brought German miners and African slaves.

The expeditions found little gold, and many Germans died of disease and in fighting. Complaints of cruelty and broken contracts led the Spanish crown to cancel the grant. It was the only German colony in the Americas of its time, an early sign of the role of European bankers in Spanish America. The province later grew around Caracas in Venezuela.
sum: Klein-Venedig, Little Venice, was the German name for the province of Venezuela when the Welser banking family of Augsburg governed it, from 1528 to 1546.
